definitions.explanation: The top surface of a building, especially when accessible.

examples.japanese: デパートの{屋上|おくじょう}に{行|い}きましょう。
examples.english: Let's go to the department store rooftop.

examples.japanese: {屋上|おくじょう}から{景色|けしき}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: You can see the view from the rooftop.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}がいいので{屋上|おくじょう}で{昼|ひる}ごはんを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: The weather was nice, so I ate lunch on the rooftop.

examples.japanese: このホテルの{屋上|おくじょう}にはプールがあって、{夏|なつ}は{泳|およ}ぐことができる。
examples.english: This hotel has a pool on the rooftop, and you can swim there in summer.

examples.japanese: {屋上|おくじょう}{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}が{満車|まんしゃ}だったので、{近|ちか}くの{別|べつ}の{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}を{探|さが}した。
examples.english: The rooftop parking lot was full, so I looked for another parking lot nearby.

notes:
{屋上|おくじょう} refers to the rooftop of a building, especially when it's accessible.

Components: {屋|おく} (roof/building) + {上|じょう} (top/above)

In Japan, many department stores (デパート) have rooftop areas with gardens, play areas, or restaurants, making {屋上|おくじょう} a familiar destination.

Common collocations:
- {屋上|おくじょう}{駐車場|ちゅうしゃじょう}: rooftop parking
- {屋上|おくじょう}{庭園|ていえん}: rooftop garden
- {屋上|おくじょう}へ{上|あ}がる: to go up to the rooftop
